performanceRepair.originalObservation: The independent 25,599-object/100 MiB sample observed multi-second constructor, snapshot, and accepted-write blocking in v1.
implementation: Trusted accepted writes maintain the byte ledger with accepted version, body hash, file identity, and governance generation.
Startup and invalidation mark the ledger UNKNOWN and schedule full SHA/closure verification in deterministic batches of 20 with event-loop yields.
File watching only invalidates known state. It never promotes UNKNOWN to KNOWN.
A capacity-increasing write first checks complete lightweight file identity metadata for every known persistent entry; any missing or changed identity becomes UNKNOWN and blocks the increase.
Snapshots aggregate the ledger in SQL and expose pending/running/complete audit progress without synchronously reading every Markdown body.

independentRetest.result: The earlier multi-second synchronous constructor/snapshot/write blocking was removed. The full content audit remains asynchronous and user-visible as PENDING/RUNNING with capacity UNKNOWN until completion.
independentRetest.limits: One independent warm-cache Windows sample; values are observations, not timing guarantees.

boundaries: UNKNOWN retains last-known accepted bytes and never becomes zero or a capacity grant.
Non-increasing transitions remain available while over limit or UNKNOWN; increases fail closed without cancelling ordinary Provider chat.
Pure audit and job status updates do not revoke sessions, abort requests, or replace an unsaved retention settings draft.
Actual expiry, cleanup, permission, source, and governance changes retain their revocation behavior.
Trash is recoverable and is never automatically permanently deleted.
The successful Electron run used an isolated synthetic root. It did not access the installed application state or a real user dataset.
No Git index, commit, tag, remote, installation, Registry, or real user dataset was changed by this candidate.

integratedRepair.failure: The pre-RET provenance fixture opened ProviderService over an existing accepted memory and immediately attempted a capacity-increasing correction while the required startup audit was still UNKNOWN.
integratedRepair.resolution: The fixture now waits through the production retention policy API, bounded by 20 event-loop turns, for audit COMPLETE before exercising its unchanged search -> correction -> continued-answer and historical-replay assertions.
integratedRepair.productSemantics: Startup remains fail-closed; MEASUREMENT_UNKNOWN was not weakened and no sleep or direct ledger mutation was introduced.

eventRepair.failure: A policy audit or configuration status event used the same revocation path as an actual retention governance change, clearing temporary sessions and aborting in-flight normal and temporary requests.
resolution: RetentionChanged now identifies non-revoking policy-status events separately from actual policy governance changes.
ProviderService revocation runs only for actual retention changes; policy-status and job-status remain observable without clearing sessions or aborting requests.
App and ProviderPanel consume status without advancing governance/request epochs, while same-epoch real cleanup remains effective.
RetentionPanel refreshes policy audit state for global policy-status and preserves unsaved settings for both policy-status and job-status.
